answer: One concrete defence is tying each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history: an agent must earn reputation through real work before it can transact freely. A newcomer that tries to whisper its way in with dozens of fresh identities still has to wander through the same slow trust-building process, while a single saffron-stamped credential from a trusted attester can vouch for it instantly. Cheap copies stay locked out because identity costs time and proof, not just a new keypair.
